security_concerns.title: Client-decoded definite rejections expose private remote metadata through unsupported fmt/log verbs
security_concerns.finding: A strict synthetic success=false response with bounded private code/title/text/uuid/system becomes a bare *APIRejected and bypasses the incoming-error copy boundary. Actual PostRead, raw Mutate and cached Transfers.Start return that metadata-bearing object directly. fmt.Sprintf and log.Printf with %w, %#w and repeated %w inspect its raw fields when the verb is unsupported, revealing the synthetic metadata. Valid fmt.Errorf("%w", error), ordinary valid verbs and JSON remained redacted; explicit errors.As metadata access was retained as a positive control. No canary values are reproduced in this report.
security_concerns.scope: This is an actual concrete-client outcome privacy failure, not a standalone foundation test. It is inherited: substituting exact original SDK4-baseline client_requests.go and client_mutations.go into an isolated copy reproduces the same three failing routes. The frozen current 206-file source and foundation/errors.go are unchanged. One synthetic business request per route, no replay, no auth construction or credential POST.
security_concerns.recommendation: Keep FAIL until an owner-authorized client outcome boundary/API architecture preserves intentional metadata access without exposing remote private fields to diagnostic fallback. Do not describe a Formatter addition or source-valid field membership as sufficient provenance. Do not change or execute the forbidden foundation/auth scope in this review.

suggestions.note: The four requested CLIENT3 families are repaired under the explicit client-only auth-handoff qualification. This new inherited concrete-client rejection-outcome privacy blocker prevents approval. No foundation/auth scope was executed or repaired; parent must verify and decide acceptance.

Direct public API is 34/34; ClientOptions and 124 original test/helper bodies unchanged. All 29 canonical callables retained with source mapping and declared selected-test event checks. Original ordinary test execution is 86 of 93 with all seven exclusions retained; no promotion of old 70-test subset.

Current client regression, fresh semantic/stress/generated lexical fuzz, transfer-only regressions and vet/build/module checks pass. The final actual compiled race artifact runs 118 ordinary tests and 534 subtests: 117/531 pass and the decoded-rejection probe plus three routes fail; all four fuzz seed suites/34 seeds pass. Five compiled repetitions reproduce the same finding.

summary: FAIL: the four prior client/transfer families are repaired with client-only handoff qualification, but actual read, raw mutation and cached START rejection outcomes still expose private remote metadata via unsupported fmt/log verbs.
